recognize_zh: A 圖血片呈雙相性，部分紅血球明顯大小不均、低色素；箭頭所指的淡色紅血球內有一團深藍色、均質圓形的包涵體（聚集的過量 α 鏈），B 圖以 methyl violet 超活體染色可見大塊紫色包涵體，符合脾切除後 β 型地中海貧血的 Fessas bodies。
features: Dimorphic red cell population with marked anisopoikilocytosis, hypochromic cells and target cells
Pale red cells containing a single large, dense, homogeneous deep-blue round inclusion (arrows)
Occasional small basophilic dots in red cells, possibly Pappenheimer or Howell-Jolly bodies post-splenectomy
Panel B: supravital methyl violet stain highlights large, dense purple intracellular inclusions (arrows)
Panel B: neutrophil and ghost-like red cells in the supravital preparation
describe_en: Composite figure. The May-Grünwald-Giemsa peripheral blood smear is dimorphic, with a population of normochromic transfused-appearing red cells and a population showing marked anisopoikilocytosis, hypochromia and target cells. Several pale red cells contain a single large, dense, round deep-blue inclusion. A supravital methyl violet preparation highlights these as large dense intracellular inclusions. In a splenectomized patient with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia, findings are consistent with Fessas bodies (precipitated α-globin chain aggregates).

ddx.vs: HbH (β4) inclusions appear as multiple fine, evenly distributed 'golf ball' dots with brilliant cresyl blue rather than one large dense aggregate.
Heinz bodies are small, peripheral, membrane-attached inclusions on supravital stain, typically with bite cells in oxidant hemolysis.
Howell-Jolly bodies are small (about 1 µm) round dark-purple nuclear remnants, much smaller than the large globin aggregates seen here.
An NRBC has a nucleus with chromatin texture and surrounding cytoplasm, whereas Fessas bodies are homogeneous, structureless inclusions in an otherwise pale cell.
